title: Cross-SDK prefetch and backpressure shim for vector paging + rerank endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers build hybrid workflows that first request dense vectors (embeddings or model vectors) for large result sets and then issue paged rerank calls. Current SDKs expose low-level paging and raw streaming APIs that differ across languages, leading to duplicated client logic (manual prefetch, naive batching, ad-hoc retries) and incorrect ordering/consistency when combining streaming + batched rerank calls.

Goal: Ship a small cross-SDK helper (prefetch + backpressure iterator + batcher) and canonical examples that provide: 1) a unified cursor-based paging primitive; 2) adaptive prefetch that respects downstream rerank concurrency and model throughput; 3) deterministic order guarantees when reranking streamed candidates; and 4) retry semantics that are safe for batched idempotent rerank calls.

Scope: Python, TypeScript, Go SDKs. Helper API surface should be idiomatic per language but parity-tested against a shared behavior spec. Ship example apps in each SDK repo under examples/vector-rerank-prefetch. Not addressing server-side changes; implement purely client-side helpers and documented best-practices for SLO-sensitive workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Define a behavior spec document that all 3 SDKs implement (cursor semantics, ordering guarantees, retry semantics)
Publish SDK helper implementing: CursorPager, AdaptiveBatcher, BackpressureIterator (or language-idiomatic names) in Python/TS/Go
Include example showing streamed vector paging -> batched rerank with deterministic global ordering in each SDK example folder
Add unit and integration tests that simulate transient network failures and verify no duplicate rerank submissions and correct ordering after retries
API ergonomics approved by DevEx and at least one PM/Design review comment addressed
Documentation page in SDK docs with code snippets and a migration note for existing users
implementation_notes: Design a small shared behavior spec in repo 'docs/sdk-behavior/vector-paging.md' and reference it in each SDK implementation
CursorPager should emit items in strict cursor order; it should expose a lookahead(prefetch_count) hook used by AdaptiveBatcher
AdaptiveBatcher groups items into batches based on dynamic latency/cost signals: target batch size default 32 but should be tunable via options
BackpressureIterator integrates with streaming responses: it must block prefetch when downstream concurrency threshold is reached to avoid exceeding model capacity

Retries: use per-batch idempotency tokens for rerank requests; on transient error, batch should be retried, but dedupe on server requires idempotency header — document fallback to at-most-once if backend does not support idempotency

Language details: Python iterator should be an async generator supporting 'aiter_prefetch(n)'; TS should provide AsyncIterable with a 'peek' method; Go should provide a channel-based iterator with context cancellation
Add metrics hooks: prefetch_latency_ms, batch_size_histogram, backpressure_wait_seconds to help Console traceability

Avoid adding new network endpoints; helpers use existing embeddings and rerank endpoints. For large result sets recommend using cursor-based server-side paging if available; helpers should be agnostic
test_plan: Unit tests: simulate pages of vectors, verify CursorPager yields correct cursor transitions and respects page_size override

Integration: scripted harness that runs example app against local sandbox service (dockerized test backend) that injects 10% transient 503s; verify no lost items and at-most-once rerank semantics where idempotency supported
Load test: run TS and Python examples with 10k items, verify memory usage grows linearly with prefetch window not dataset size, and that adaptive batcher stabilizes around target latency
Cross-SDK parity tests: run behavior spec test-suite against each SDK implementation; tests are stored in 'sdk-tests/vector-paging-suite' and executed in CI matrix
End-to-end acceptance: PM to run example and confirm UX accepts default options and comments on ergonomics
qa_checklist: Docs updated with code samples for all 3 languages
Examples added to each SDK repo under examples/vector-rerank-prefetch
Reviewer signoff from DevEx: @sophia-k or @noah-m in PR reviews
Performance regressions measured and added to Console dashboard for the example project
Security review: confirm idempotency token usage does not leak PII in logs
